A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SANA-Sprint and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, Appendices A–F, and references. Full text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable matching without material gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original MJHQ-30K and GenEval results, component ablations, inference and training analyses, and qualitative ControlNet outputs.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and appendix analyses, with revised benchmark values and one replacement qualitative example.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendices A–C retain the same Flow-to-TrigFlow transformation, dense time embeddings, QK normalization, hybrid sCM/LADD objective, max-time weighting, and ControlNet extension.

E1.justification: Training-data coverage, MJHQ-30K, GenEval, and HED-conditioned ControlNet tasks are unchanged. Figure 4 substitutes an illustrative prompt within the existing qualitative text-to-image coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same comparator rows. Figure 4 still compares SANA-Sprint with SDXL-LCM, SD3.5-Turbo, SDXL-PCM, SDXL-DMD2, and FLUX-schnell.

E3.justification: The reported metrics, training budgets, hardware, batch sizes, and inference timestep schedules remain unchanged, including Appendix F.1 and Table 7. No revised quantitative evaluation setting accompanies the changed Table 2 scores.

E4.justification: Figure 4 replaces the one-step Luffy example with a blue-suede handbag example across all six methods, revising the qualitative case comparison for fidelity and prompt alignment. Section 4.3 and Appendix F.2 ablations and sensitivity analyses are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports evaluation seed or repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Statistical and uncertainty-reporting practices remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 2 revises SANA-Sprint 1.6B under unchanged reported settings: four-step FID/CLIP changes from 6.66/28.38 to 6.54/28.45; two-step from 6.76/28.32 to 6.50/28.45; and one-step FID/CLIP/GenEval from 7.59/28.00/0.74 to 7.69/28.27/0.76. Other table entries are unchanged. Figure 4 also replaces one row of qualitative outputs.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, objectives, Proposition 3.1, and its derivation and proof in Appendix D are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same hybrid-distillation, unified sampling, efficiency, and interactive-generation claims. The headline 7.59 FID and 0.74 GenEval values also remain unchanged despite Table 2's revisions.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations, ablation interpretations, training-instability discussions, and applicability statements are unchanged. No explanation reconciles the revised benchmark values with the retained narrative.

D1.justification: The first-page Links line adds an HF Models hyperlink to a model collection, providing an additional access pointer. Code/project links and implementation, hardware, and hyperparameter disclosures are otherwise unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 5, the expanded related work in Appendix E, and the reference list are unchanged. No cited work or research-positioning argument is added or removed.

P1.justification: v3 changes author order, removes the Project Lead designation, corrects Miyang Li to Muyang Li in the acknowledgements, and updates dates and link wording. The scientific prose and section organization are otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 4 replaces six one-step images and their prompt while retaining its grid, caption, and placement. Table 2 adjusts ranking emphasis around revised values. Other figures, tables, and appendix layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added model-access link is useful, but v3 introduces inconsistencies absent in v1: the abstract and Figure 1 retain 7.59 FID/0.74 GenEval while Table 2 reports 7.69/0.76, and Section 4.2 retains two-step FID 6.76 versus the table's 6.50. These unreconciled revisions modestly weaken the reliability of the central performance reporting.
